data.name: Akshu
data.gender_notes: Akshu is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Akshu represents the divine eye or the third eye, symbolizing perception, intuition, and wisdom. The name is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Aksh' meaning 'eye'. The name Akshu carries the meaning “Divine Eye, Perception” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Akshu usually hope their child will grow to embody divine eye, perception and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of inner vision and enlightenment.
data.etymology: Akshu belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Divine Eye, Perception.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Akshu total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Akshu is deeply rooted in Hindu culture as a symbol of divinity, particularly associated with the divine eyes of various deities like Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati. In Hindu rituals, the application of tilak or vermilion powder on the forehead to signify the 'third eye' is done to seek blessings and protection.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, the third eye is considered a symbol of enlightenment and spiritual awareness, representing the inner vision and intuition that helps one gain wisdom and knowledge beyond physical senses. The name Akshu is believed to bestow upon its bearer the qualities of insight, perceptiveness, and deep understanding, making it a spiritual and significant name in Hindu culture.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Akshu: Eyes of the Soul. In Hinduism, the inner eye or third eye is the gateway to spiritual knowledge and inner wisdom. Akshu symbolizes the awakened inner vision, guiding one towards self-realization and enlightenment.

historical_references.reference: Akshu was a revered sage in ancient Hindu texts, including the Mahabharata and Puranas. He was a disciple of the sage Angiras and is believed to have lived during the Vedic period.

Akshu is also mentioned in the Jain literature as a Tirthankara or Jina, who is believed to have lived during the Avasara or Arhat period. He is said to have attained kevala jnanam (omniscience) and led many souls to salvation.
historical_references.time_period: Avasara or Arhat Period (c. 8th century BCE - 2nd century CE)
